conviction_note: The fundamental read is a beat: the company has topped its own revenue-guide midpoint by 5.8-9.5% in each of the last four quarters, so I expect about +6.5% against a $224.8M bar. The reaction read is a coin flip leaning slightly down. The stock is at an all-time high, up 19.4% in 20 days, with six price-target raises into the print and a sell-side average target ($114) below spot ($117.44). Puts are bid: skew +5.57 and put/call OI 3.14. The last beat-and-raise bought only +1.7%, and a 10% holder is selling under a 10b5-1 plan. The print will turn on the Q4 implied guide and the first 2027 commentary, not on the Q3 beat. So p_up is 47 on an abs move of 14 (-0.84). The findings sum to -1.3. The two measurements agree in sign and roughly in size.
bar: Q3 2026 revenue consensus $224.8M from two agreeing estimate sources: Stocktwits ($224.78M, EPS $0.58, https://stocktwits.com/symbol/HNGE/earnings) and Benzinga ($224.8M, EPS $0.55, https://www.benzinga.com/quote/HNGE/earnings-forecasts). Chartmill is higher at $229.05M (https://www.chartmill.com/stock/quote/HNGE/estimates). The company guide is $223-225M revenue and $61-63M non-GAAP operating income (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001673743/000162828026052558/hnge-q2202684xex991.htm). FY2026 guide is $856-860M revenue and $236-244M non-GAAP operating income. The FY guide less Q1 ($182.3M), Q2 ($212.8M) and the Q3 guide midpoint ($224M) implies a Q4 of about $239M. The published consensus sits on the guide, and the buy-side whisper is unsourced (the beat history points to $237-245M).
positioning_check: Short interest is 6.33M shares, 3.3 days to cover, as of the 2026-09-30 settlement (https://massive.com/quote/hnge, captured 2026-10-26). An earlier reading was 6.0M shares and 4.0 days (2026-08-19, https://equibles.com/stocks/hnge/shortinterest). Against 62.47M Class A shares outstanding (Form 144, 2026-10-14) that is about 10% of the Class A count: elevated but not a crowded short in the 18-23% range that squeezed before. The skew is +5.57 vol points, put/call OI 3.14 and total OI 9,540, so downside protection is paid. Part of the put OI may be hedges against the long run-up and the Insight distribution. The stock is at its 52-week high (+276.8% off the low), up 19.41% in 20 days and 5.13% in 5 days. The options-implied event move is 13.34% (straddle 15.07%).

findings.finding: Hinge has beaten the midpoint of its own revenue guide by 5.8-9.5% in each of the last four quarters: Q3'25 $154.2M vs 141-143; Q4'25 $170.7M vs 155-157; Q1'26 $182.3M vs 171-173; Q2'26 $212.8M vs the June-raised 200-202 (194-196 originally). The same habit on the Q3'26 guide of $223-225M gives about $237-245M, 6-9% over the $224.8M published consensus, which sits on the guide.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: A revenue beat has not reliably paid. Q2'26: a 5.8% beat over the raised guide, a FY raise and the Cylinder deal bought +1.73%. Q3'25: an 8.6% beat sold off -15.06%. Q4'25 (+9.5% beat) and Q1'26 (+6% beat) rose +17.28% and +10.23%, both with large guide raises.
findings.why_not_priced: Published consensus ($224.8M at two sources) still sits on the guide, so the beat is not in the printed bar. The buy side almost certainly models it, though: four straight beats, Chartmill estimates revised up 7.75% in three months, and the stock up 19% into the print. If the beat were unexpected, the stock would not be at an all-time high with six target raises in October. So the beat itself is only a small positive. A beat below about 5% would read as a miss.
findings.independence: The Q4'25 beat is in a separate document: https://www.chartmill.com/news/HNGE/Chartmill-41655-HINGE-HEALTH-INC-A-NYSEHNGE-Crushes-Q4-Estimates-and-Provides-Strong-2026-Guidance. So is the Q2'26 deck, which notes win rates up y/y and an active pipeline ahead of last year: https://s205.q4cdn.com/978984498/files/doc_financials/2026/q2/Hinge-Health-Earnings-update-Q2-2026.pdf

findings.finding: The Q4 guide is the line that decided this name's reactions. In Nov 2025 Hinge guided Q4 to $155-157M, flat on a $154.2M Q3 (Q4 later printed $170.7M), and the stock fell 15.06% on an 8.6% beat. The current FY guide implies a Q4'26 of about $239M, flat-to-down on a Q3 likely printing $237-245M. Unless FY is raised by more than the Q3 beat plus the $7-8M Cylinder contribution, the implied Q4 will look like a sequential stall against a stock priced for acceleration.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: A conservative, flat-sequential Q4 guide in Nov 2025 was followed by -15.06%. The strong initial FY guide in Feb 2026 bought +17.28%. A $34-38M FY raise in Aug 2026 bought only +1.73%.
findings.why_not_priced: A Q4 guide is new information released only with the print. With the stock at an all-time high and the sell-side average target ($114) already below spot, the market is pricing a raise well beyond the mechanical Q3 flow-through. A conservative Q4 habit that the street has learned to look through would leave the stock unmoved on a cautious guide; the Nov 2025 -15% says it has not always done so.
findings.independence: The Nov 2025 -15.06% reaction is reported independently at https://finviz.com/news/221556/hinge-health-hnge-sheds-15-after-swinging-to-net-loss, which attributes it to a GAAP net loss rather than the guide, so the guide reading is my inference. The current implied Q4 is arithmetic on the Aug 2026 8-K (separate document).

findings.finding: Expectations went up hard into the print. The stock is up 19.41% in 20 days to a 52-week high of $117.44, up about 91% YTD. Stifel ($130), BofA ($130), KeyBanc ($140) and Barclays ($110) raised targets in October and BofA reinstated at Buy. Even so, the 17-analyst average target of $114.31 sits below spot, and the option market pays for downside: skew +5.57, put/call OI 3.14.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The last print came after a run-up into a beat-and-raise and moved only +1.73% (Aug 2026). Before the Nov 2025 -15.06%, the stock had recovered toward its post-IPO highs.
findings.why_not_priced: This is the price itself, so it is priced by definition. The point is that it raises the bar the guide has to clear. The skew already agrees with this sign, so it is sized small.
findings.independence: The AAII price report (close $113.90 on 2026-10-27, up 17.13% in October, three upgrades and no downgrades in a month): https://www.aaii.com/investingideas/article/541632-why-hinge-health-inc8217s-hnge-stock-is-up-521. The baseline skew and P/C OI are a separate source.

findings.finding: Insight Venture Partners, a 10% holder, is distributing under a 10b5-1 plan adopted 2026-08-20. On 2026-10-14 one fund (Insight Venture Partners (Cayman) X) filed a Form 144 for 614,262 Class A shares (~$64.5M), after 725,357 shares (~$69.2M) sold in the prior three months. Sister funds filed parallel 144s the same day and on 2026-09-30 and 2026-09-01. That supply continues through the window at about a third of average daily volume (1.87M shares).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: None isolated. The stock rose about 17% in October while this plan was selling.
findings.why_not_priced: Form 144s are public, and the stock has absorbed this supply on the way up, so most of it is priced. It is filed because pre-scheduled plan selling caps any post-print squeeze and gives a weak guide an extra seller.
findings.independence: The co-investor fund's parallel 144 (17,825 shares, same plan date): https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1673743/000197407826000382/primary_doc.xml (same filer family, so not independent). The EDGAR filing list shows 23 Form 144s and 17 Form 4s since 2026-08-28.

findings.finding: Short interest of 6.33M shares (about 10% of 62.47M Class A shares, 3.3 days to cover, 2026-09-30) is up from 6.0M in August. A strong FY raise would meet a short base big enough to add a few points to an up-move.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: In Feb 2026 the stock rose +17.28% on a strong guide. Short interest at that time is unknown.
findings.why_not_priced: Short covering is conditional on a positive guide surprise, and the market cannot pre-price a conditional squeeze. At 3.3 days it is moderate, so it is sized small.

findings.finding: The Cylinder Health acquisition ($105M cash) closed on 2026-09-01. The Q2 deck guided $7-8M of Cylinder revenue in 2026, and the 8-K does not say whether the $856-860M FY range already includes it. Roughly $2M lands in Q3 and $5-6M in Q4. That adds mechanically to any FY raise; GI program costs are in guidance, with the launch in 2027.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The deal was announced with the Q2 print, which moved +1.73%. Its effect cannot be isolated.
findings.why_not_priced: If Cylinder was excluded from guidance, part of the FY raise is inorganic, and the market may discount it once that is disclosed. The amount (about 1% of FY) is too small to matter much either way.
findings.independence: The company newsroom lists 'Hinge Health officially welcomes Cylinder Health' on 2026-09-01 (via search, https://www.hingehealth.com/resources/press-releases/q3-earnings-date/ newsroom listing).

findings.finding: The Q2 deck says 2027 bookings are building: 'active pipeline ahead of last year', win rates up y/y, a 300K-life Fortune 15 takeaway, SMB lives up more than 100% in H1, surgery clients signed for a 2027 launch, and an opt-out partnership adding clients from 2027. The Q3 call is the first read on the 2027 selling season, which is what a stock at an all-time high is paying for.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Feb 2026: a strong initial year guide on a selling-season read bought +17.28%.
findings.why_not_priced: The direction was disclosed in August and the run-up reflects it. Its size (client adds for 2027, booked lives) is first quantified on this call. If the market already had a number, the October target raises would cite one. They cite profitable growth and AI narrative instead.
findings.independence: MarketBeat's summary of the Q2 call also reports the ~300,000-life enterprise win and the opt-out partnership (https://www.marketbeat.com/earnings/reports/2026-8-4-hinge-health-inc-stock/). It covers the same call, so it is not independent.

findings.finding: On 2026-08-18 Hinge signed a new 119,278 sq ft San Francisco lease at 300 Mission Street through Feb 2037, with about $86.0M aggregate base rent (about $8M a year) and a $2.8M letter of credit. That is a headcount-expansion signal, and the opex is immaterial against $236-244M of FY non-GAAP operating income.
findings.why_not_priced: Public 8-K and immaterial. It matters only if the call frames 2027 margin around hiring or GI and migraine investment, a risk analysts flagged after Q2.

baseline_tension: What I found agrees with the skew and cuts against the run-up. The run-up and the target raises say the beat-and-raise is expected, the put skew says downside is being bought, and nothing found suggests a guide large enough to beat that bar, which is why p_up sits only slightly below 50 rather than lower.
lessons_applied: Lesson 1 (a verified fact is not a predicted reaction): the beat-pattern finding cut from +1.0 to +0.5, because the last 5.8% beat-and-raise bought only +1.73% and the Q3'25 beat sold off 15%

Lesson 3 (own caveat reaches the number): the Q4-guide finding cut from -1.5 to -1.0, because the street may now look through a conservative Q4 guide after four straight beats, and finviz attributes the Nov 2025 drop to GAAP rather than the guide
Lesson 6 (verify the bar): bar confirmed by two agreeing sources ($224.8M) plus the company guide, so no cap
Lesson 7 (positioning): short interest checked at about 10% of Class A and 3.3 days, not crowded; the negatives agree with the skew, so they are left as sized
Lesson 8 (understatement): abs_move_pct raised from 13.0 to 14.0, between the 13.3% implied and the 15.1% median reaction, with a guidance change likely; p_up kept at 47
